newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's reservoirs fill up after recent rains.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's reservoirs fill up after recent rains.

text.p: Water levels in Morocco's reservoirs rose to 7.07 billion cubic metres after falling to 2.30 billion cubic metres last year when the country suffered its worst drought on record, the ministry of public works said on Thursday.
"After the recent winter rains, which soaked nearly the whole country, water stock has substantially improved compared with last year," the ministry said in a bulletin.
The reservoirs were up to 71.7 percent of their total capacity compared with 23.3 percent in 1995, it said.
Water stock in Morocco's main reservoirs, Bin El-Widane and Oued El-Makhazen, has reached 80 percent and 63.6 percent respectively of capacity, the ministry said.

Last year's drought, described by the government as " the drought of the century", cut the 1995 grain harvest to 1.6 million tonnes, one fifth of an average year and way below 1994's exceptional harvest of 9.4 million tonnes.
Morocco has more than 60 large and medium-size dams that provide water to irrigate an estimated 890,000 hectares, officials said.
The authorities plan to extend the irrigated surface to a total of 1.0 million hectares by the year 2000. --Rabat newsroom +212-7 726518
